questions.prompt: A case contains several tickets involving the same employee. How should their evidence be read?

options.text: Use each ticket's stated time, operation and facts without importing unshown outcomes
options.explanation: A shared name does not make all snapshots one completed transaction.

options.text: A success in one ticket resolves every other ticket
options.explanation: Different boundaries and attempts need separate results.

options.text: The latest narrative automatically rewrites archived evidence
options.explanation: Archived incidents retain their explicitly supplied timing.

options.text: Every hypothetical proposal has already executed
options.explanation: Proposed work and observed outcomes differ.

questions.prompt: One SP node rejects K2 while another accepts SAML but fails account matching. What is established?

options.text: There are separate trust-adoption and identity-resolution mismatches
options.explanation: Different evidenced boundaries need their own corrections and retests.

options.text: A key rollback necessarily fixes the account mapping
options.explanation: Signing-key selection does not redefine the emitted subject.

options.text: Every failed page must have one common cause
options.explanation: Similar symptoms can hide distinct failures.

options.text: The successful node proves all users are healthy
options.explanation: A node's acceptance does not establish every account outcome.

evidence: Node A trusts K2, accepts SAML, then finds no account for the emitted identity
Node B lacks approved K2 and rejects verification
Both are fresh attempts with distinct request IDs

questions.prompt: HR department and the Okta user profile are correct, but the app profile is wrong. Where is the first evidenced data mismatch?

options.text: Between the correct user profile and the app-specific value
options.explanation: Investigate the actual mapping and application-profile update path.

options.text: Inside HR necessarily
options.explanation: The supplied HR value is correct.

options.text: At the final report permission necessarily
options.explanation: The data already differs before that downstream resource decision.

options.text: In every source relationship
options.explanation: One demonstrated mismatch does not establish universal sourcing failure.

review.heading: Explain the architecture in ordinary language

questions.prompt: Okta issues a response and the SP rejects the wrong audience. What is the justified conclusion?

options.text: Issuance succeeded but receiver targeting acceptance failed
options.explanation: An upstream success cannot override a local validation rejection.

options.text: The user necessarily typed the wrong password
options.explanation: The supplied failure is later than issuer processing.

options.text: Every target account is missing
options.explanation: No target account-lifecycle result is supplied.

options.text: The audience check should be removed to restore service
options.explanation: That would discard the intended trust boundary.

questions.prompt: A SAML sign-in succeeds while a separate SCIM update is rejected. How should the analyst report it?

options.text: Successful sign-in and failed account-data update as separate outcomes
options.explanation: Protocol operations have distinct responsibilities and results.

options.text: Declare the SCIM update successful because entry worked
options.explanation: Application entry does not establish account-update completion.

options.text: Declare every sign-in failed because SCIM rejected
options.explanation: The supplied sign-in outcome remains successful.

options.text: Treat both as the same browser POST
options.explanation: The delivery and operation types differ.

evidence: Separate SAML attempt: accepted and local session created
SCIM account update: rejected by target
No later successful target update is supplied

questions.prompt: A proposed import match finds two candidates with similar identifiers. What is appropriate?

options.text: Resolve ownership and matching ambiguity before confirming association
options.explanation: Choosing a convenient record risks linking the wrong identity.

options.text: Pick the account with the newest login
options.explanation: Recency is not sufficient ownership evidence.

options.text: Merge accounts merely because names resemble each other
options.explanation: Similarity is not an approved unique match.

options.text: Create a duplicate to avoid investigation
options.explanation: Another record does not resolve the ambiguity.

questions.prompt: An enabled reader reaches projects, then is denied an admin change as required. What needs repair?

options.text: No defect is demonstrated by that expected denial
options.explanation: Authentication and allowed reading can coexist with correct administrative restriction.

options.text: Promote the reader to administrator
options.explanation: That would violate the supplied requirement.

options.text: Replace the provider's signing key
options.explanation: A local expected authorization result is not a verification failure.

options.text: Delete the user's app account
options.explanation: No account-eligibility problem is established.

questions.prompt: A leaver is deactivated in Okta while one target's termination is unconfirmed. How should the status be recorded?

options.text: Confirmed provider change with that target outcome still open
options.explanation: Do not extend an upstream result into an unverified downstream claim.

options.text: Complete removal everywhere
options.explanation: The target result is explicitly unconfirmed.

options.text: Definite failure at every target
options.explanation: Missing one result does not prove universal failure.

options.text: No issue can exist until a cause is known
options.explanation: An open required outcome matters even before its cause is established.

review.heading: Close the request without hiding an unknown

questions.prompt: A mapping uses the wrong transformation but its authoritative input is correct. What should a justified plan target?

options.text: The demonstrated transformation and its supported application/update behavior
options.explanation: Fix the evidenced boundary rather than changing correct business facts.

options.text: Rewrite the authoritative value to fit the wrong output
options.explanation: That falsifies correct source information.

options.text: Change all policy rules in the org
options.explanation: That is unrelated and unnecessarily broad.

options.text: Disable the entire identity platform permanently
options.explanation: The packet supports a specific mismatch, not universal failure.

questions.prompt: A node's effective trust lacks approved K2. What remains unknown from that inventory alone?

options.text: Why the approved update was not adopted there
options.explanation: Observed state identifies a mismatch, but not its operational root cause.

options.text: Whether the node lists K2
options.explanation: The supplied inventory establishes its absence.

options.text: Whether K2 was intended to be approved
options.explanation: That approval is part of the stated facts.

options.text: Whether an arbitrary embedded certificate should be trusted
options.explanation: Incoming material does not create independent approval.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
evidence: Approved plan: node B should trust K2
Effective node B inventory: K1 only
Reason for missing adoption: not supplied

questions.prompt: Which plan best tests a repaired integration across two active nodes?

options.text: Fresh attempts at both nodes with actual trust, identity, session and permission evidence
options.explanation: One node's result does not prove the other adopted the correction.

options.text: Only one old session at either node
options.explanation: That can bypass the changed path.

options.text: Only a central configuration screenshot
options.explanation: Saved state is not every runtime's effective behavior.

options.text: Only confirm the app's public home page loads
options.explanation: Public availability is not identity acceptance evidence.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is most defensible in a case handover?

options.text: Named evidence, confirmed boundaries, remaining unknowns, proposed correction and verification status
options.explanation: A good summary separates facts, hypotheses, actions and observed outcomes.

options.text: The cause is obvious, with no evidence references
options.explanation: Confidence alone does not support a diagnosis.

options.text: All issues share the most recent change
options.explanation: Temporal proximity does not prove a universal cause.

options.text: A proposed fix is already a verified recovery
options.explanation: Execution and retest evidence are still required.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

questions.topic: Challenge: Two nodes require two boundary diagnoses
questions.prompt: Fresh attempts hit two active SP nodes after a signing-key change. Which investigation summary preserves the supplied results?
evidence: Node A: approved key trusted, SAML accepted, account resolution fails
Node B: approved key absent, verification fails before account resolution
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, state the last confirmed success and the first evidenced gap. What in the packet supports each?

options.text: A has an account-resolution gap; B has an earlier trust gap
options.explanation: The same user-facing failure masks different stopping points. Keep each node's correlated attempt separate and plan correction and verification for each evidenced boundary.

options.text: Both nodes have only a NameID issue because neither user entered
options.explanation: Node B did not reach account resolution; a shared symptom cannot establish the same cause.

options.text: Both nodes need only the signing key because the change was recent
options.explanation: Node A already verifies and accepts SAML. Its evidenced remaining gap is different.

options.text: Node A success proves the deployment is complete across the service
options.explanation: Node A has an unresolved local-account result, and Node B has an independent verification failure.

questions.topic: Challenge: An action without an outcome is unfinished
questions.prompt: A final handover includes one verified repair and one submitted target action. Which outcome remains unknown?
evidence: Mapping incident: intended target value confirmed corrected
Leaver incident: target deactivation requested; no target result or access test supplied
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, name the exact missing outcome. Separate it from facts that the packet already supplies.

options.text: Whether the required leaver target removal actually completed
options.explanation: A verified result in one incident does not close another. Track the target operation and required access checks under the leaver incident's owner.

options.text: Whether the mapping incident has a verified corrected target value
options.explanation: The packet explicitly confirms that result.

options.text: Whether a leaver target action was requested
options.explanation: The request is supplied; execution and effect are the missing outcomes.

options.text: Whether these incidents have different evidence statuses
options.explanation: Their statuses are supplied. The unresolved engineering outcome is target removal.

review.heading: Close the request without hiding an unknown

questions.topic: Challenge: Prioritize an evidenced continuing exposure
questions.prompt: Two tickets are open. Which next action best follows the explicitly supplied impact?
evidence: Ticket A: reader can read; forbidden administration is denied as required
Ticket B: departed worker's old app session still reads sensitive records after the required immediate cutoff
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, explain which uncertainty your next check would resolve and why the other actions are premature.

options.text: Prioritize B's continuing exposure; record A's denial as expected
options.explanation: B demonstrates a missed removal requirement with continuing protected access. A demonstrates the intended permission boundary, not a repair need.

options.text: Prioritize removing A's denial because every denial is a failure
options.explanation: A's denied action is explicitly prohibited; changing it would weaken the approved boundary.

options.text: Close B because central deactivation would normally be enough
options.explanation: The observed continuing target access contradicts closure of the stated immediate-cutoff requirement.

options.text: Treat both as equivalent authentication failures
options.explanation: A is an expected authorization result; B concerns continuing access after removal. Neither supports that combined diagnosis.

questions.prompt: An integration repair addresses wrong audience configuration and inconsistent node trust. Which verification record most strongly supports closing those defects?
evidence: Service: two active SP nodes; approved key K15 and audience urn:projects:prod
Requirements: intended users enter; wrong-audience responses remain rejected; local reader limits remain
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, describe the evidence that would show success and the relevant failure or rejection that should remain.

options.text: Verify fresh per-node behavior, intended entry and required rejection cases
options.explanation: This tests deployment consistency, the repaired boundary and relevant authorization behavior. Name the attempt, node and outcome rather than relying on one service-wide success label.

options.text: Record one successful refresh through whichever node the load balancer chooses
options.explanation: A refresh can use an old session and leaves the second node's new-entry behavior unverified.

options.text: Record that the key and audience are present in the design document
options.explanation: The document expresses intent; it does not establish effective configuration or runtime results on both nodes.

options.text: Record that rejection disappeared after disabling all validation
options.explanation: That avoids the acceptance requirements instead of proving the authorized repair and expected denials.

review.heading: Close the request without hiding an unknown
